criteria_note: Guide criteria A-F, G, X1, T1-T3 scored 0-10. Claims checked against current docs.vllm.ai pages (quickstart, installation, GPU, CPU, engine args, arch overview, docker, helm, CLI), v0.6.4 engine args, chart values.yaml and v1 scheduler.py on GitHub, the arXiv HTML and vLLM blog posts. Prose length excludes front matter, headings, code, display math, tables, images and the Sources list. Single judge run.

A.reason: TL;DR then problem -> PagedAttention -> sharing -> V1 architecture -> scheduler -> install -> args -> CPU -> Helm -> choice; good arc. Deductions: near-empty section L147-149 '### V1에서 기본으로 켜지는 해시 기반 프리픽스 캐싱' holds one generic sentence ('운영 관점에서 보면 ... 이득이 커집니다') and never explains hashing; TL;DR L17 '기본 구성은 세 종류의 프로세스' vs L165 '네 종류로 나뉩니다'; L605 caption-only paragraph '위 그림은 vLLM의 Helm 배포 아키텍처를 나타냅니다.'

B.reason: Natural 입니다 register, varied sentences. Nits: L296 '숫자가 클수록 우선순위가 낮다는 점을 착각하기 쉬우므로' (noun frame; -> '숫자가 클수록 우선순위가 낮으니 헷갈리기 쉽습니다'); L320 '같은 방향의 설정으로 볼 수 있습니다' (hedging formula); L233 '기준으로 삼으면 됩니다'.

C.reason: Broken back-references: L537 '텐서 병렬을 켜면 앞서 본 것처럼 `|`로 rank마다 코어 구간을 나눕니다' (the | syntax was never shown); L575 '오프라인·온라인 기본값은 앞서 소개한 `world_size` 배수 값입니다' (never introduced, values missing); L100 version note on block manager dropped in without connection; L147 stub section breaks the prefix-caching flow.

D.reason: Help lands at hard points: 300/2048 waste arithmetic L35, 500-token/4-sample block count L122, process-count function L195-213, token-budget toy scheduler L251-285 with traced output, NUMA 30+40>64GiB example L533. Little padding.

E.reason: OS-paging mapping table L47, blockwise attention formula L58-60, process table L176, policy table L291, comparison table L687; figures placed at discussion. Deductions: L603-605 Helm diagram with a one-line caption only; prefix-caching section has no visual or mechanism where one would help.

F.reason: 31 of 33 checked claims supported. Deduction: L480 '기본값은 `0.92`입니다' omits that the default is 1.0 with the extensible KV cache (Engine Args). L575 claims defaults it does not state. L696 2.2x/4.3x lacks the ShareGPT trace scope.

G.reason: use_math true with $$ present, description 127 chars and longer than title, Liquid wrapped in raw (L629), fences single-word, paired $$.

X1.reason: Categories Tech Guides/Language-Models; 7 tags, mostly specific; 'Efficient-Attention' is loosely fitting (PagedAttention targets memory management, not attention FLOPs).

T1.reason: Install, offline, serve, curl/openai, Docker, source build, CPU env, Helm commands all runnable in order; toy code runs and its stated outputs match (3/6/17; {'A':1,'B':1,'C':14}). Gaps: CPU batched-token defaults missing L575; chunked prefill flag given without default.

T2.reason: Covers the quickstart plus paper/blog internals in a sensible order; Helm/CPU sections are supported by official pages. Minor: Unsloth advice is a thin addition.

T3.reason: Explains PagedAttention, CoW, beam trees, V1 process architecture, TP step, token-budget scheduler, preemption, version differences named as v0.6.4, and when vLLM wins or loses (L679-714). Gap: hash-based prefix caching mechanism promised but not explained.

preference.reason: Both are factually strong (X 1 unsupported of 32, Y 0 of 32). X follows the guide shape the protocol asks for: TL;DR, internals and the current V1 process architecture before installation, and a closing on when to choose vLLM and where it falls short. Its defects are local: one stub section and two broken back-references. Y is more operationally thorough and runnable (tuning, observability, benchmarking, DP modes) with accurate cross-references, but it has no TL;DR, buries internals after ~470 lines of install material, omits the V1 architecture, and ends without an assessment. Moderate margin.
